bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-26.

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers conducting controlled substance research and affects the regulatory classification of chemical substances.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect prosecution and defense of drug trafficking cases.
Universities and research institutions conducting controlled substance research would be subject to the new registration processes and requirements established by the bill.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and relaxes some requirements for research facilities working with controlled substances.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the Forest Service to transfer approximately 233 acres of federal land in Arizona's Tonto National Forest to Gila County at no cost, provided the county requests it and uses the property to serve veterans. The county must pay all transfer costs, including surveys and environmental reviews. If the land stops being used for veterans' purposes, ownership would revert to the federal government.

bill.title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against the Republic of Cuba that have not been authorized by Congress.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.

industries.rationale: The resolution would directly affect military deployment decisions and operational scope for defense contractors supporting U.S. forces in the region.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would require the President to withdraw U.S. military forces from any hostilities in or against Cuba unless Congress has formally declared war or authorized the use of force. The measure includes exceptions allowing the U.S. to defend itself from attack or imminent attack, and to continue lawful counternarcotics operations. It addresses the constitutional balance between executive and legislative authority over military deployments.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-1.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

plain.whoItTouches: People applying to live here, and their families here. People applying to come here, and their families here.

bill.title: Patients Deserve Price Tags Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 522.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services
Drug safety, medical device, and laboratory regulation

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new price-disclosure obligations on hospitals and surgical centers, changing their administrative and compliance requirements.
Medical device costs must be included in the price estimates, affecting how device manufacturers' products are priced and disclosed to patients.
Price transparency requirements may affect how insurers negotiate rates and how patients understand their coverage and out-of-pocket costs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require hospitals, ambulatory surgical centers, and other healthcare facilities to provide patients with upfront price estimates for scheduled procedures and services. The estimates would need to include costs for the facility, physicians, anesthesia, medical devices, and other associated charges. Facilities that fail to provide these price disclosures could face civil penalties.

industries.rationale: The prior authorization model directly affects hospitals and physician groups by requiring advance approval for certain Medicare services they provide.
Third-party contractors processing prior authorization requests are typically health insurers or related entities that would lose revenue from this model's termination.
The model specifically requires enhanced technology and artificial intelligence systems for processing authorization requests, affecting technology vendors serving the healthcare sector.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would block a Medicare pilot program that began in January 2026 in six states. The program requires third-party contractors to use enhanced technology, including artificial intelligence, to review and approve certain Medicare services before they are provided. The contractors are paid based on a share of any savings generated. This resolution would stop the program from continuing.

bill.title: Holocaust Education and Antisemitism Lessons Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 470.
subjects: War crimes, genocide, crimes against humanity

industries.rationale: The bill directs a study of curriculum requirements and instructional materials used in public schools, directly affecting education publishers and curriculum developers who produce Holocaust education materials.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum to conduct a study and report to Congress on how Holocaust education is taught in public elementary and secondary schools across the country. The study would examine whether states and local school districts require Holocaust education, what standards and curriculum requirements exist, and what instructional materials are being used. The bill does not itself mandate Holocaust education or change school curricula; it only requires the museum to gather and report information on current practices.

bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly exempts family farms from asset calculations for federal student aid eligibility.
The bill changes how federal student aid eligibility is calculated, affecting aid distribution and potentially enrollment patterns.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restore an exemption that allows families to exclude the value of their farm or small business (with 100 or fewer employees) when applying for federal student aid. Recent changes to the financial aid application began counting these assets when determining how much aid a student qualifies for, starting in the 2024-2025 school year. The bill would return to the previous policy of not counting these family-owned farms and businesses as assets in the aid calculation.

districtAwards.description: PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE OF THIS GRANT IS TO SUPPORT CLOSING THE BROADBAND AVAILABILITY GAP AND SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF A FIVE-YEAR ACTION PLAN.THE PROPOSED PROJECT INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING PLANNING AND PRE-DEPLOYMENT ACTIVITIES: RESEARCH AND DATA COLLECTION, INCLUDING INITIAL IDENTIFICATION OF UNSERVED LOCATIONS AND UNDERSERVED LOCATIONS CONSISTENT WITH RULES, REGULATIONS, AND PROCESSES COMMISSION HAS ESTABLISHED FOR MAKING DETERMINATIONS IN BROADBAND DATA MAPS; THE DEVELOPMENT OF A PRELIMINARY BUDGET FOR PRE-PLANNING ACTIVITIES; ASSET MAPPING ACROSS THE ELIGIBLE ENTITY TO CATALOGUE BROADBAND ADOPTION, AFFORDABILITY, EQUITY, ACCESS AND DEPLOYMENT ACTIVITIES OCCURRING WITHIN THE ELIGIBLE ENTITY; ESTABLISHING, OPERATING, OR INCREASING CAPACITY OF A BROADBAND OFFICE THAT OVERSEES BROADBAND PROGRAMS AND BROADBAND DEPLOYMENT IN AN ELIGIBLE ENTITY; REASONABLE POST-NOFO, PRE-AWARD EXPENSES <$100,000 RELATING TO PREPARATION OF PROGRAM SUBMISSIONS OR ADDING ADDITIONAL CAPACITY IN PREPARATION FOR BEAD PROGRAM EXPECTED OUTCOMES: THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF ARIZONA'S PROJECT, "ARIZONA'S BEAD PLAN (ABP)" ARE A FIVE-YEAR ACTION PLAN RESULTING IN A COMPREHENSIVE BROADBAND PLAN FOR THE STATE OF ARIZONA; EXPANDING THE STATE'S DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE STATEWIDE TO IMPROVE THE ECONOMY AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR ALL ARIZONANS, IDENTIFYING AND PRIORITIZING SHORT TERM AND LONG TERM BROADBAND PROJECTS, AND CONVENING PARTNERS AND LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS TO ALIGN ON A COMMON, SHARED GOAL OF PROVIDING AFFORDABLE, RELIABLE, AND HIGH-SPEED INTERNET FOR ALL ARIZONIANS. THE BEAD PROGRAM FUNDING WILL SUPPORT ARIZONA'S STRATEGIC PLANNING EFFORTS TO OFFER RELIABLE BROADBAND SERVICE TO UNDERSERVED AND UNSERVED AREAS OF THE STATE.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES ARE UNSERVED AND UNDERSERVED GROUPS IN THE STATE OF ARIZONA WITH A FOCUS ON RURAL AND UNSERVED POPULATIONS.SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES: THE RECIPIENT DOES NOT INTEND TO INTEND TO SUBAWARD FUNDS.
